data.body:
COMPLETION VERIFICATION FAILED with 6 unmet criteria, and it was RIGHT about one of them. Not
force-closing. Correcting the record and re-verifying.

## The real finding: I overclaimed one criterion

"A ticket whose events change between prep and the locked re-check is skipped cleanly" is NOT
implemented — and does not need to be. I ticked every AC with a bulk script, which is exactly
how an untrue claim gets into a ticket. The gate caught it. Verified by reading the merged
code, not by memory: `compact_txn.py` contains no event-set re-check, and the only thing
hoisted out of the lock is `_sweep_position_map` (`compact.py:451`).

The design changed during implementation, correctly. The plan proposed hoisting the whole fold
(parse, reduce, ledger) out of the lock and re-checking the event set under it. What shipped is
narrower: only the HISTORY WALK moved out, built once per sweep before any lock is taken, while
the fold still runs entirely inside `_compact_locked`. That removes the git-log cost from the
critical section — the entire point of the ticket — without splitting the locked section, so no
prep/commit window exists and there is nothing to re-check. I have rewritten that criterion to
say so explicitly and marked it SUPERSEDED rather than deleting it, so the change of design
stays visible in the record.

## The other four are real evidence the verifier's search missed

Each of these tests exists in the merged tree at 50cc45f0d1 in
`tests/unit/test_compact_sweep_perf.py` (413 lines, added by that commit — confirmed with
`git show --stat` and `git cat-file -e`):

| criterion | test |
|---|---|
| ledger unchanged by the optimisation | `test_ledger_is_identical_with_and_without_a_prebuilt_map` (:233) |
| map argument optional, fsck rebuild unaffected | `test_the_map_argument_is_optional_for_the_rebuild_path` (:252) |
| commit contains only folded paths | `test_the_sweep_commit_does_not_steal_a_concurrent_writers_event` (:290) |
| sweep stands aside mid-run | `test_the_sweep_yields_when_a_writer_takes_the_lock_mid_run` (:351) |

And the two the verifier did find, plus one more:
`test_a_sweep_walks_history_once_regardless_of_ticket_count` (:154),
`test_the_single_ticket_path_still_builds_its_own_map` (:179),
`test_no_history_walk_runs_while_the_store_lock_is_held` (:198),
`test_a_failed_map_build_degrades_to_per_ticket_not_per_event` (:380).

Eight tests, all passing locally on the merged commit, all RED-verified against the pre-fix
code with counted reverts.

## Why the bug is resolved end to end

The sweep now performs ONE `git log` walk, built before any lock, instead of one per ticket
inside the lock — and the deployed reality was worse than one-per-ticket, since per-ticket map
misses fell through to per-EVENT wildcard walks (`'*<event-id>*.json'`, captured by the pony
lane; a leading wildcard defeats pathspec pruning so each is a full-history scan).
`test_a_sweep_walks_history_once_regardless_of_ticket_count` asserts `sweep_map == 1`,
`ticket_map == 0`, `per_event == 0` and `per_position == 0`, so it fails if ANY event falls
through to that wildcard walk. `test_no_history_walk_runs_while_the_store_lock_is_held` asserts
the structural claim directly by sampling lock-dir presence at each walk.

Mirror lag is not a factor: 50cc45f0d1 is present on both `gerrit/main` and `origin/main`, and
the test file is in that tree.
